title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

title: Awakening Awareness: Embracing This Moment
description:
The Mindful Stream (CA)
A session inspired by Eckhart Tolle's practices. Feel free to join as we get still and practise presence within this moment. We will discuss and observe the obstacles that, seemingly, block us from being present and bring awareness to our unconsciousness in a safe, inclusive and affirming way.

Sessions are suitable for newcomers, those experienced in Tolle's teaching and anyone wishing to remain completely anonymous.

See you there!

Please be aware that sessions will close if no members have joined after 10 minutes.

Emrys has been passionate about mindfulness since 2010 and since 2021 he has been organising free, weekly online meditation groups. For more information on his free Work of Byron Katie online mediation group, visit [this Meetup Group link](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/).

title: Mindfulness Tuesday Meditation: Cultivating Consciousness
description:
Meditate with a Monk in Sonoma County
Join us for a transformative workshop on mindfulness meditation and cultivating consciousness. Dive deep into the teachings of Theravada Buddhism, focusing on insight meditation to develop a clear understanding of the nature of the mind and consciousness. This workshop will include guided meditation sessions to help you strengthen your meditation practice and cultivate mindfulness in your daily life. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced meditator, this workshop offers a welcoming space to explore the depths of your own consciousness and enhance your spiritual journey. Come together with like-minded individuals to deepen your practice and connect with the wisdom of Theravada Buddhism.
Our sessions are led by Bhikkhunis closely associated with our Dhammadharini Sangha. Check out Dhammadharini Sangha at [https://www.dhammadharini.net/](https://www.dhammadharini.net/)
Register for this event on Dhammadharini's website:
[https://www.dhammadharini.net/event-details/tuesday-evening-meditation-dhamma-talk-2](https://www.dhammadharini.net/event-details/tuesday-evening-meditation-dhamma-talk-2)

title: UPDATE: 1st Wednesday! Wednesday Night Walk start at STARBUCKS  on the East Side
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma East Side Green Belt

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at STARBUCKS at the leghorn shopping center, and walk about 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we walk at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: STARBUCKS
* Distance: \~ 4.5 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat
* Optional After-walk gathering at
* WHAT TO BRING:
* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

Gary
SCO Organizer

title: Free Estate Planning Webinar
location: https://mackaydressler.com/workshops
description:
Creating your estate plan, whether it’s a living trust or a will, can be a daunting task. Estate planning addresses issues that are difficult to think about, such as death, incapacity, finances, and family dynamics. It can be easy to procrastinate, even though these issues may weigh heavily on your mind.

We invite you to attend one of our upcoming free webinars so you can take the first step toward having peace of mind by creating (or updating) your estate plan. This is an educational webinar, where we highlight some of the concerns that many families face and how an estate plan can help. The attorneys also break down how wills and trusts differ, and some of the common estate planning pitfalls and how to avoid them.

Our goal is to provide you with the education you need to protect yourself and your family, and leave a legacy of peace. If you would like to set up a meeting to discuss your estate planning needs further, we offer all participants who complete the webinar a free, no obligation personal consultation with one of the attorneys.

At this webinar, we will discuss several common issues and concerns, including:

* The advantages and disadvantages of wills, living trusts, and probate
* Protecting your children’s inheritance from their future ex-spouses, lawsuits, and other claims
* Most living trusts fail; if you already have a trust, find out what you can do to ensure that it will protect you and your loved ones
* How to preserve your nest egg for your family if you find yourself needing Long Term Care
* How to stay out of court and avoid the cost, time, and stress that a conservatorship can bring if you become incapacitated.

Attend a webinar and receive a FREE no-obligation consultation with an Attorney to answer any questions about setting up your estate plan ($550 value).

description:
Petaluma Figure Drawing Meetup Group
# [Crit Group At Suite G Studio](https://www.suitegstudio.com/eventscalendar/crit-group)

*With Guest Moderator: Petaluma Public Art Specialist- Melissa Abercrombie*

* Thursday, May 7, 2026
* 6:00 PM 9:00 PM

**Why Create Art in a Vacuum?**

Join us at Suite G Studio for our first group critique. Each artist brings one to two (within the same series) pieces, either finished or in progress, to receive feedback from other artists and a guest professional moderator. This is a fun, engaging, relaxed atmosphere to talk about your work, get the perspectives from fellow artists, while having the opportunity to learn about their work practices.
Each artist will have a 10-15 minute slot in which the moderator and artists discuss their work. They will be given 5 minutes at the end of their crit to discuss or explain their work.
Cost $30
Space is limited to 10 participants. To reserve your spot you can Venmo @suiteg $30, or [BECOME A MEMBER](https://www.suitegstudio.com/artist-resources)! for $40/month, come to all drawing groups and other events for free. However, you must still [RSVP](suitegstudio620@gmail.com) to hold your spot.

More About Melissa Abercrombie
Melissa Abercrombie is a creative fueled by community engagement. She holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Painting and Printmaking from San Francisco State University and brings artistic vision, passion, and civic commitment to every project. Her tenure as chair of the Petaluma Public Art Committee, along with service on multiple city commissions, informs her work as a Public Art Specialist focused on integrating art into public spaces and expanding opportunities for artists and residents to engage in creative expression.
Melissa’s leadership is reflected in her contributions to a diverse portfolio of public art projects that animate the City of Petaluma and strengthen its cultural identity. As the staff liaison to the Petaluma Public Art Committee, she has guided the Lucchesi Skatepark Public Art RFP for an upcoming youth-centered installation. She project-managed *Scent Me Back*, a narrative mural by Rough Edge Collective at the Petaluma Teen Center that connects memory and place, and oversaw the selection and installation of *Slough Birds*, an environmental artwork honoring local ecology by Jonny Hirschmugl. She also partnered with artist Michael Garlington to develop *True Heart of Petaluma: Ode to the Petaluma Fairgrounds #1*, a photo mural celebrating civic pride during a period of transition at the Fairgrounds. Additionally, she project-managed *Woven Stories*, an installation by Rude Calderón and Roberto Delgado amplifying Native community voices on a junior high campus.

title: Historic Petaluma River Cruise
location: Petaluma River
description:
A scenic, narrated journey exploring the Petaluma River’s history, wetlands, and wildlife.

Friday, May 8  4:00-6:00 PM
Purchase Tickets Here

The Petaluma Museum and Dolphin Charters invite you to step aboard for a relaxing and enriching cruise along the Petaluma River—where history, ecology, and community come together.
In connection with Time & Tide: An Artful Exploration of Petaluma’s Wetlands, this special outing offers a unique opportunity to experience the landscapes featured in the exhibition from the water itself. As you travel through the heart of the Petaluma watershed, you’ll gain a deeper understanding of how the river and its wetlands have shaped the region over time—and how they continue to support wildlife, agriculture, and climate resilience today.
Expert guides will share insights into the river’s past and present, from its role in early settlement and industry to ongoing restoration efforts that are helping rebuild vital wetland habitats. Along the way, keep an eye out for birds and other wildlife that depend on this rich and dynamic ecosystem.
Your ticket includes drinks, appetizers, and engaging narration in a beautiful, open-air setting.
Whether you’ve visited the exhibit or are simply curious about the river, this cruise offers a memorable way to connect with Petaluma’s natural and cultural history.
18 and over please. Departure location and details will be shared separately.

title: Petaluma River History Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Petaluma River History Paddle The Petaluma River is the reason there’s a city here. Long before highways and railroads, this tidal waterway was the region’s saltwater highway —a working river that powered Petaluma’s rise and connected Sonoma County’s farms and businesses to San Francisco, the Gold Rush, and markets around the world. On this two-hour, gentle guided paddle , history comes alive through storytelling from multiple points of view. You’ll paddle in stable sit-on-top kayaks with an experienced, costumed guide, while costumed actors on shore step into the lives of real Petalumans who once depended on the river for their livelihood. Hear stories from people who worked the egg trade, ran messages between businesses, managed boarding houses, and built enterprises that fueled a growing city. As you move through downtown and along historic riverbanks, you’ll gain a deeper appreciation for the ingenuity, industrious spirit, and daily lives that shaped Petaluma—and the river that made it all possible. No paddling experience necessary. All equipment and instruction provided. Just bring your curiosity—and be ready to see Petaluma through new eyes. $75/person. Includes everything, even insight! Founded 88 years ago, the Petaluma Danish Soldiers Club has quietly been part of Petaluma’s cultural and civic life for nearly a century. Located on Kastania Road, the club has long served as a gathering place for people of Danish and Scandinavian heritage, and for the wider community. You’re invited to visit us from 11:00 am to 2 pm. At 11:30 am, Club President Tim Knudsen will give a short presentation on the club’s history.

Come visit this largely hidden in plain sight building and institution in Petaluma. The Club President, Tim Knudsen, will offer a short presentation on the club’s history and its role in the community at 11:30 am. Lunch will be served at 12:30 p, if interested. If you plan to stay for lunch, and we truly hope you can, please purchase your meal seven days in advance. There is no option to purchase lunch tickets on the day of the event, and no outside food is permitted.

title: Petaluma Watershed Demonstrations
location: Petaluma Historical Library & Museum, 20 4th St, Petaluma, CA, United States
description:
Discover how water connects our landscape with Petaluma Wetlands Alliance docents.

Recurring:
Demonstrations on Saturday, May 9  from 12:00 – 3:00 pm
Demonstrations on Saturday, June 6 from 12:00 – 3:00 pm
Please Make Your Reservations Here

On select Saturdays, a docent from the Petaluma Wetlands Alliance will be at the Petaluma Museum to lead family-friendly, drop-in demonstrations exploring the flow of water through the Petaluma River watershed—and how it shapes the wetlands featured in the exhibit Time & Tide: An Artful Exploration of Petaluma’s Wetlands.

Visitors will learn how water moves from hills to river to bay, and how these connections influence habitat, water quality, and climate resilience.
Admission to the Museum is a suggested $5 donation per person. Watershed demonstrations are free. RSVPs appreciated!

title: Mindfulness Sunday Meditation: Cultivating Consciousness
description:
Meditate with a Monk in Sonoma County
Join us for a transformative workshop on mindfulness meditation and cultivating consciousness. Dive deep into the teachings of Theravada Buddhism, focusing on insight meditation to develop a clear understanding of the nature of the mind and consciousness. This workshop will include guided meditation sessions to help you strengthen your meditation practice and cultivate mindfulness in your daily life. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced meditator, this workshop offers a welcoming space to explore the depths of your own consciousness and enhance your spiritual journey. Come together with like-minded individuals to deepen your practice and connect with the wisdom of Theravada Buddhism, and provide an opportunity to deepen mindfulness, wisdom, and inner stillness.
Our sessions are led by Bhikkhunis closely associated with our Dhammadharini Sangha. Check out the [recording from the past event](https://youtube.com/live/s07U2kzWoWk?feature=share) on our YouTube channel.
You’re also welcome to join us in person at Dhammadharini Monastery, in the peaceful setting of our outdoor Dana Sala Pavilion
Register for this event on Dhammadharini's website to receive the address:
[https://www.dhammadharini.net/event-details/sunday-morning-guided-meditation-questions-2](https://www.dhammadharini.net/event-details/sunday-morning-guided-meditation-questions-2)

title: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Mother’s Day SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River, “Petaluma’s Longest Park” Hey, MOM! We know what you want. Peace and quiet. Time to reflect. Time to not reflect. Time to float. Time to flow. Step away from the rush and into the quiet of the Petaluma River for a peaceful SUP Yoga experience with The Floathouse Petaluma . We’re moms too. We know…. Though we launch from the heart of downtown, the central turning basin offers a surprisingly serene setting—calm water, open sky, and a sense of ease that feels far removed from daily life. This all-levels, 90-minute session is designed for everyone: experienced yogis, seasoned paddle boarders, and complete beginners alike. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board (knees are always welcome). Once we reach our practice spot, we anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. From there, you’re invited to move, breathe, rest, or simply be—guided by an experienced instructor and supported by the shared rhythm of water and community. All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards measuring 34 inches wide and 11 feet long—much larger than a yoga mat and designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water. Come as you are. Choose your own level of effort. Flow with the river and the people around you. You deserve it. It’s YOUR river. Come out and play. $50/person, includes all gear, instruction, and quality time on the water. title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

title: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan
description:
Petaluma Book (And Brew) Club
2014: At a dinner for close friends and colleagues, renowned poet Francis Blundy honors his wife's birthday by reading aloud a new poem dedicated to her, 'A Corona for Vivien'. Much wine is drunk as the guests listen, and a delicious meal consumed. Little does anyone gathered around the candlelit table know that for generations to come people will speculate about the message of this poem, a copy of which has never been found, and which remains an enduring mystery. 2119: Just over one hundred years in the future, much of the western world has been submerged by rising seas following a catastrophic nuclear accident. Those who survive are haunted by the richness of the world that has been lost. In the water-logged south of what used to be England, Thomas Metcalfe, a lonely scholar and researcher, longs for the early twenty-first century as he chases the ghost of one poem, 'A Corona for Vivian'. How wild and full of risk their lives were, thinks Thomas, as he pores over the archives of that distant era, captivated by the freedoms and possibilities of human life at its zenith. When he stumbles across a clue that may lead to the elusive poem's discovery, a story is revealed of entangled loves and a brutal crime that destroy his assumptions about people he thought he knew intimately well.

title: Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown & Riverfront
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown and Riverfront

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at Aqus Cafe and take in the West Side of town, including some of Downtown, the Waterfront and a few of the Historic home of old Petaluma. We walk about 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

Afterward if you have the time, join us at Aqus Cafe for a bite to eat and some liquid refreshment before heading home. Aqus Cafe is a true gem of a gathering place, restaurant, coffee house, and live music venue. But it's the people on either side of the counter that make this place so special.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: Aqus Cafe
* Distance: 3.5 to 4-1/2 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat with a few small and easy to climb hills
* Optional After-Hike Gathering at Aqus Cafe

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

Gary
SCO Organizer

title: Insect Discovery Lab
location: Shollenberger Park, 1400 Cader Lane, Petaluma, 94954, United States
description:
Explore the small but mighty creatures of the wetlands and other ecosystems!

Saturday, May 16 10:00am – 11:00 am
Please Make Your Reservations Here

In connection with Time & Tide: An Artful Exploration of Petaluma’s Wetlands, the Petaluma Wetlands Alliance invites families to a special hands-on program exploring the small but mighty creatures of the wetlands and other ecosystems.
Join educators from SaveNature.org for a free Insect Discovery Lab on Saturday, May 16, from 10–11 AM at the Shollenberger Park Gathering Circle.
San Francisco–based SaveNature is dedicated to inspiring awareness and participation in the preservation of fragile ecosystems through direct engagement with the natural world.
Young explorers will discover the fascinating world of arthropods while meeting beetles, millipedes, hissing cockroaches, walking sticks, and more. This interactive experience introduces budding scientists to the incredible diversity of insects in our wetlands—and their essential role in the web of life.
Space limited to 25 children with parents. Grades K–12. RSVP required.

title: Upstream High Tide Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Upstream High Tide Paddle [High Tide: ~5.4 feet] When the tide rises, the river reveals a hidden world. Join The Floathouse crew for a gentle, guided paddle upstream on a high tide of 5.4 feet , when the Petaluma River opens into its quieter, greener reaches. With extra water beneath us, we’re able to glide beyond the downtown channel and into a tranquil tidal slough—an ever-changing habitat rich with birdlife and natural beauty. Book your upstream adventure here. ($60/person includes gear, guide and nature’s awesomeness.) As we drift upstream, keep an eye out for great egrets, blue herons, snowy egrets, turtles basking along the banks , and the lush plant life that thrives where freshwater and tides meet. The pace is unhurried, the water is calm, and the experience is deeply grounding—many guests say they can feel their stress melt away within minutes. Along the way, our guide shares stories of the flora, fauna, and human history that have shaped this upper channel—from its ecological importance to its role in Petaluma’s past as a working river. You’ll come away with a deeper appreciation for how close this wild place is to the heart of downtown. ✨ Beginner-friendly 🚣 Sit-on-top kayaks 🌊 High tide access makes this route possible 🌿 A peaceful, nature-forward experience Come explore the Petaluma River at one of its most magical moments—when the tide is high, the river is deep, and the wild feels wonderfully close. title: Downriver Run with Optional Sauna Refresh Sesh
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Downriver Run + Optional Sauna Refresh Sesh 📅 Saturday, May 16 ⏰ Downriver Run: 3-5 pm. Optional Sauna + Cold Plunge: 5-6:30 pm Go with the flow. Ride the tide. Find the vibe. Join the crew from The Floathouse for a one-way, two-hour glide downriver in Hobie pedal kayaks—powered by your legs and the outgoing tide. This slow-lane journey follows the Petaluma River south of town, slipping quietly through hidden wetlands and tidal habitat that most people never see, and that can’t be accessed any other way. As the tide carries you along, you’ll pedal approximately six miles , moving effortlessly through a living landscape of reeds, birds, and broad skies. Egrets lift off ahead of you, herons stand sentinel along the banks, and the river widens into its wilder self. Along the way, we’ll share stories of this working tidal slough—its ecology, its rhythms, and why this stretch of river matters. At the finish, reward yourself with the optional Refresh Sesh at Sundrop Sauna . Step into the heat, rinse, reset, and leave feeling energized—inside and out. Beginner-friendly. Unforgettable. Be part of nature—and let the tide do the work. Book here. ($85 for downriver run, $125 for downriver run + sauna refresh sesh) Includes all gear, snacks and drinks at the sauna, and sauna & cold plunge experience. Bring towel, swimming suit, slides. Hobie pedal kayaks provided. Transportation details, meeting point, and sauna timing shared after registration. title: Spike Sikes and His Awesome Hotcakes: Salute to American Graffiti Edition
location: Hall of the Above,199 Petaluma Boulevard North, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Stick around after Cruisin' the Boulevard for this special show from Spike Sikes!

--

Like hotcakes themselves, the music Spike’s Awesome Hotcakes plays goes by many names. Soul. Swing. Rhythm & Blues. Jazz. Jump.

Just The Right Recipe… The most frequently heard comment after a Spike’s Awesome Hotcakes gig goes something like this –

“No one is making this kind of music anymore!”

But what, exactly, is “this kind of music?”

Like hotcakes themselves, it goes by many names. Soul. Swing. Rhythm & Blues. Jazz. Jump. It’s a sound that’s classic and simple, but when it’s done right, it hits the spot, and has you grinning from ear to ear. Spike has spent years searching for this sound.

From the Texas blues joints he cut his teeth in to the funky halls of New Orleans, he was always studying the music, trying to find just the right recipe. It makes perfect sense that he found his bandmates in Sonoma County, a music scene that has fostered many eclectic artists for decades.

What he didn’t know was how hungry audiences were for “this kind of music.” You might say they’ve been eating it up like…Hotcakes!

🍸 We will have a cash bar serving alcoholic drinks, mocktails and other beverages.

Tickets here https://www.eventbrite.com/e/spike-sikes-and-his-awesome-hotcakes-tickets-1984347404504?aff=oddtdtcreator

title: SRJC Bands: Pandora's Box
location: Burbank Auditorium - Santa Rosa Campus
description: Symphonic Band & Jazz Band take a critical look at what humans are doing to our world. Feat. Video Projections, Erik Johnson & Jazz Mirage.  The SRJC Symphonic Band and Jazz Band take a critical look at what humans are doing to our world.  Who are we are a country? How do we get along? Is there room for everybody? title: Mindfulness Sunday Meditation: Cultivating Consciousness
description:
Meditate with a Monk in Sonoma County
Join us for a transformative workshop on mindfulness meditation and cultivating consciousness. Dive deep into the teachings of Theravada Buddhism, focusing on insight meditation to develop a clear understanding of the nature of the mind and consciousness. This workshop will include guided meditation sessions to help you strengthen your meditation practice and cultivate mindfulness in your daily life. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced meditator, this workshop offers a welcoming space to explore the depths of your own consciousness and enhance your spiritual journey. Come together with like-minded individuals to deepen your practice and connect with the wisdom of Theravada Buddhism, and provide an opportunity to deepen mindfulness, wisdom, and inner stillness.
Our sessions are led by Bhikkhunis closely associated with our Dhammadharini Sangha. Check out the [recording from the past event](https://youtube.com/live/s07U2kzWoWk?feature=share) on our YouTube channel.

title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

title: Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown & Riverfront
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown and Riverfront

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at Aqus Cafe and take in the West Side of town, including some of Downtown, the Waterfront and a few of the Historic home of old Petaluma. We walk about 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

Afterward if you have the time, join us at Aqus Cafe for a bite to eat and some liquid refreshment before heading home. Aqus Cafe is a true gem of a gathering place, restaurant, coffee house, and live music venue. But it's the people on either side of the counter that make this place so special.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: Aqus Cafe
* Distance: 3.5 to 4-1/2 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat with a few small and easy to climb hills
* Optional After-Hike Gathering at Aqus Cafe

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

Gary
SCO Organizer

title: Turn to The River: A Guided Paddle through The Past, Present, & Future of an Iconic Sonoma County Waterway
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA 94952
description: Turn to The River: a guided paddle tour The future is NOW for the Petaluma River, the historic Sonoma County waterway credited for the birth, growth, and lasting relevance of the charming Bay Area city of Petaluma, California. Just 40 miles north of San Francisco, let us take you on a journey through the past, present, and future of the long & winding “saltwater highway” that brought Petaluma to life and continues to support how we live and play today. This tidal slough—the Petaluma River —inspired generations of immigrants to conceive of industrial and pastoral innovations that shaped the history of the entire San Francisco Bay area and beyond. From the days of the Gold Rush to the present moment, the Petaluma River has beckoned miners and farmers, industrialists and solopreneurs, visionaries and ecologists to imagine new ways of interacting with this place. It remains an ever-changing connector between wetlands and city, land and water, past and future. Book your seat today on this fascinating guided kayak tour —$75 per person includes all gear, an experienced guide, and post-paddle perks at local businesses. title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!

title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

title: Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown & Riverfront
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown and Riverfront

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at Aqus Cafe and take in the West Side of town, including some of Downtown, the Waterfront and a few of the Historic home of old Petaluma. We walk about 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

Afterward if you have the time, join us at Aqus Cafe for a bite to eat and some liquid refreshment before heading home. Aqus Cafe is a true gem of a gathering place, restaurant, coffee house, and live music venue. But it's the people on either side of the counter that make this place so special.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: Aqus Cafe
* Distance: 3.5 to 4-1/2 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat with a few small and easy to climb hills
* Optional After-Hike Gathering at Aqus Cafe

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

Gary
SCO Organizer

description: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River, “Petaluma’s Longest Park” Step away from the rush and into the quiet of the Petaluma River for a peaceful SUP Yoga experience with The Floathouse Petaluma . Though we launch from the heart of downtown, the central turning basin offers a surprisingly serene setting—calm water, open sky, and a sense of ease that feels far removed from daily life. This all-levels, 90-minute session is designed for everyone: experienced yogis, seasoned paddle boarders, and complete beginners alike. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board (knees are always welcome). Once we reach our practice spot, we anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. From there, you’re invited to move, breathe, rest, or simply be—guided by an experienced instructor and supported by the shared rhythm of water and community. All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards measuring 34 inches wide and 11 feet long—much larger than a yoga mat and designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water. Come as you are. Choose your own level of effort. Flow with the river and the people around you. It’s YOUR river. Come out and play. $50/person, includes all gear, instruction, and quality time on the water. title: Plein Air Paint Out
location: Ellis Creek Water Recycling Facility, 3890 Cypress Drive, Petaluma, PA, 19454, United States
description:
A relaxed and inspiring morning of outdoor painting at one of Petaluma’s most beautiful wetland landscapes.

Saturday, May 31 8:00am – 12:00 pm

Please Make Your Reservations Here

Held in connection with the Petaluma Museum’s exhibitTime & Tide: An Artful Exploration of Petaluma’s Wetlands, this community paint out invites artists of all levels—from beginners to experienced plein air painters—to gather, observe, and create in the open air.
Painting outdoors—en plein air—offers a unique way to connect with the landscape. At Ellis Creek, you’ll experience shifting light, birdlife, and the quiet movement of water while capturing the wetlands through your own creative lens.
Whether you’re trying plein air painting for the first time or are a seasoned artist, this is a welcoming, low-pressure opportunity to slow down, observe, and create in community.
Good to Know:
Morning light is ideal, and we recommend arriving between 8:00–9:00 AM, with painting continuing through noon.
Ellis Creek offers free parking, restrooms, scenic views right from the lot, and easy access to painting spots near the ponds and along the trails.
The parking lot for the Ellis Creek Water Recycling Facility is close to 3882 Cypress Dr. Petaluma, CA 94954. GPS Coordinates: The main parking lot is at 38 13 35N, 122 35 08W approximately.
Guided instruction is not provided, but there will be opportunities for informal guidance, tips, and shared learning from fellow painters throughout the morning.
What to Bring:
A simple plein air kit might include:

Portable easel (French easel or pochade box)
Painting surface (8×10″ or 9×12″ panels or watercolor block)
Paint (oils, acrylics, or watercolor)
Brushes and/or palette knife
Water or solvent container (with lid)
Pencil for sketching
Paper towels or rags
Folding chair or stool
Sun protection (hat, sunscreen, umbrella)
Drinking water

Optional:

Wet panel carrier or wax paper for transport
Spray bottle (acrylics) or masking tape (watercolor)

title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma East Side Green Belt

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at STARBUCKS at the leghorn shopping center, and walk about 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we walk at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: STARBUCKS
* Distance: \~ 4.5 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat
* Optional After-walk gathering at
* WHAT TO BRING:
* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

title: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: SUNSET SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River, “Petaluma’s Longest Park” Step away from the rush and into the quiet of the Petaluma River for a peaceful SUP Yoga experience with The Floathouse Petaluma . And float into the sunset with us. Time to say goodbye to the week. Though we launch from the heart of downtown, the central turning basin offers a surprisingly serene setting—calm water, open sky, and a sense of ease that feels far removed from daily life. This all-levels, 90-minute session is designed for everyone: experienced yogis, seasoned paddle boarders, and complete beginners alike. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board (knees are always welcome). Once we reach our practice spot, we anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. From there, you’re invited to move, breathe, rest, or simply be—guided by an experienced instructor and supported by the shared rhythm of water and community. All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards measuring 34 inches wide and 11 feet long—much larger than a yoga mat and designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water. Come as you are. Choose your own level of effort. Flow with the river and the people around you. It’s YOUR river. Come out and play. $50/person, includes all gear, instruction, and quality time on the water. title: Learn to SUP: Build skills. Find flow. Love the river.
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Learn to SUP: Build Skills. Find Flow. Ready to feel confident on a paddleboard? Our Learn to SUP class is a welcoming, two-hour introduction designed to help you paddle smarter — not harder — so you can truly enjoy your time on the water. Start your SUP journey here. For just $60 , you’ll learn from an ACA-certified (American Canoe Association) instructor in a small, supportive group of just 2–6 students . That means personalized attention, real feedback, and space to grow. We’ll cover: Proper stance and balance Efficient paddle technique Turning and maneuvering Launching and returning to the dock River awareness and safety basics Many people hop on a board and think they’re having fun — but they’re working twice as hard as they need to. This class unlocks the “aha” moments that make paddleboarding smoother, more efficient, and way more enjoyable. title: Downriver Run with Optional Sauna Refresh Sesh
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Downriver Run + Optional Sauna Refresh Sesh 📅 Sunday, June 14⏰ Downriver Run: 3-5 pm. Optional Sauna + Cold Plunge: 5-6:30 pm Go with the flow. Ride the tide. Find the vibe. Join the crew from The Floathouse for a one-way, two-hour glide downriver in Hobie pedal kayaks—powered by your legs and the outgoing tide. This slow-lane journey follows the Petaluma River south of town, slipping quietly through hidden wetlands and tidal habitat that most people never see, and that can’t be accessed any other way. As the tide carries you along, you’ll pedal approximately six miles , moving effortlessly through a living landscape of reeds, birds, and broad skies. Egrets lift off ahead of you, herons stand sentinel along the banks, and the river widens into its wilder self. Along the way, we’ll share stories of this working tidal slough—its ecology, its rhythms, and why this stretch of river matters. At the finish, reward yourself with the optional Refresh Sesh at Sundrop Sauna . Step into the heat, rinse, reset, and leave feeling energized—inside and out. Beginner-friendly. Unforgettable. Be part of nature—and let the tide do the work. Book here. ($85 for downriver run, $125 for downriver run + sauna refresh sesh) Includes all gear, snacks and drinks at the sauna, and sauna & cold plunge experience. Bring towel, swimming suit, slides. Hobie pedal kayaks provided. Transportation details, meeting point, and sauna timing shared after registration. Note: Most folks arrange for their own transportation back to town, but with advance notice, one of our staff members or volunteers can give you a ride. #block-d5c574a17fbb82ea0f13 { --tweak-text-block-radius: 0px 0px 0px 0px; --tweak-text-block-radius: unset; --stroke-style: none;--stroke-thickness: 6px; --tweak-text-block-background-color: initial; } #block-d5c574a17fbb82ea0f13 .sqs-html-content { --tweak-text-block-padding: 6% 6% 6% 6%; --tweak-text-block-padding: initial; } #block-d5c574a17fbb82ea0f13 { mix-blend-mode: var(--tweak-text-block-blend ); } #block-d5c574a17fbb82ea0f13 { } @media screen and (max-width: 767px) { #block-d5c574a17fbb82ea0f13 { } } @media screen and (max-width: 767px) { #block-d5c574a17fbb82ea0f13 .sqs-html-content { } } @media screen and (max-width: 767px) { }

title: Upstream High Tide Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Upstream High Tide Paddle [High Tide: ~6.2 feet] When the tide rises, the river reveals a hidden world. Join The Floathouse crew for a gentle, guided paddle upstream on a high tide of over six feet , when the Petaluma River opens into its quieter, greener reaches. With extra water beneath us, we’re able to glide beyond the downtown channel and into a tranquil tidal slough—an ever-changing habitat rich with birdlife and natural beauty. Book your upstream adventure here. ($60/person includes gear, guide and nature’s awesomeness.) As we drift upstream, keep an eye out for great egrets, blue herons, snowy egrets, turtles basking along the banks , and the lush plant life that thrives where freshwater and tides meet. The pace is unhurried, the water is calm, and the experience is deeply grounding—many guests say they can feel their stress melt away within minutes. Along the way, our guide shares stories of the flora, fauna, and human history that have shaped this upper channel—from its ecological importance to its role in Petaluma’s past as a working river. You’ll come away with a deeper appreciation for how close this wild place is to the heart of downtown. ✨ Beginner-friendly 🚣 Sit-on-top kayaks 🌊 High tide access makes this route possible 🌿 A peaceful, nature-forward experience Come explore the Petaluma River at one of its most magical moments—when the tide is high, the river is deep, and the wild feels wonderfully close. title: Petaluma River History Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Petaluma River History Paddle The Petaluma River is the reason there’s a city here. Long before highways and railroads, this tidal waterway was the region’s saltwater highway —a working river that powered Petaluma’s rise and connected Sonoma County’s farms and businesses to San Francisco, the Gold Rush, and markets around the world. On this two-hour, gentle guided paddle , history comes alive through storytelling from multiple points of view. You’ll paddle in stable sit-on-top kayaks with an experienced, costumed guide, while costumed actors on shore step into the lives of real Petalumans who once depended on the river for their livelihood. Hear stories from people who worked the egg trade, ran messages between businesses, managed boarding houses, and built enterprises that fueled a growing city. As you move through downtown and along historic riverbanks, you’ll gain a deeper appreciation for the ingenuity, industrious spirit, and daily lives that shaped Petaluma—and the river that made it all possible. No paddling experience necessary. All equipment and instruction provided. Just bring your curiosity—and be ready to see Petaluma through new eyes. $75/person. Includes everything, even insight! description:
Petaluma Urban Chat has launched The Vacancy Project, a bold new effort to tackle long-standing empty storefronts and underused lots in the heart of the city. At the center is an interactive, community-built Vacancy Map highlighting over 40 vacant properties within a half-mile of downtown—bringing visibility to an issue that’s been hiding in plain sight.

These spaces represent more than empty buildings. They mean lost opportunities for housing, local businesses, and a thriving downtown.

Now it’s time to take the next step.

* RSVP https://www.tickettailor.com/events/urbanchat/2174223 to join the conversation and help shape the future of downtown Petaluma.

Join us for a free community organizing meeting to turn insight into action. We’re bringing together residents, property owners, and local leaders to identify solutions, shape priorities, and begin building a shared roadmap to activate these spaces and bring new life to downtown Petaluma.

The event is free, and we ask that you RSVP https://www.tickettailor.com/events/urbanchat/2174223 in advance to be part of the conversation.

title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!

description: Learn to SUP: Build Skills. Find Flow. Ready to feel confident on a paddleboard? Our Learn to SUP class is a welcoming, two-hour introduction designed to help you paddle smarter — not harder — so you can truly enjoy your time on the water. Start your SUP journey here. For just $60 , you’ll learn from an ACA-certified (American Canoe Association) instructor in a small, supportive group of just 2–6 students . That means personalized attention, real feedback, and space to grow. We’ll cover: Proper stance and balance Efficient paddle technique Turning and maneuvering Launching and returning to the dock River awareness and safety basics Many people hop on a board and think they’re having fun — but they’re working twice as hard as they need to. This class unlocks the “aha” moments that make paddleboarding smoother, more efficient, and way more enjoyable. Held right in the heart of downtown Petaluma on the beautiful Petaluma River, this is your chance to build skills in a calm, supportive environment — and start feeling at home on the water. Bring a friend, learn together, and find your flow. All equipment included. Only 6 paddlers per class. title: Full Strawberry Moon Paddle/Pedal
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA 94952
description: 🍓 Strawberry Moon Paddle / Pedal Sunday, June 28, 2026 | 7:30–9:30 pm Join us for a warm summer evening on the Petaluma River under the Strawberry Moon , a name shared by many Native American cultures to mark the season of ripening fruit, blooming plants, and new life. This guided nighttime paddle in Hobie pedal kayaks is playful, easy, and perfect for lingering summer light and rising moonshine. Pedal along with your community as the river reflects the glow of early summer. June’s Full Moon is known by many names, each rooted in seasonal rhythms: Strawberry Moon — Algonquin, Ojibwe, Dakota, and Lakota peoples; the time when wild strawberries were ready to gather Berries Ripen Moon — Haida; marking the ripening of fruits Blooming Moon — Anishinaabe; celebrating peak flowering season Green Corn Moon — Cherokee; signaling the tending of crops Hoer Moon — Western Abenaki; associated with agricultural work Hot Moon — An 18th-century term recorded by Captain Jonathan Carver, reflecting early summer heat Birth Moon — Tlingit; the season when animals give birth Egg Laying Moon / Hatching Moon — Cree; marking new life emerging across the land These names remind us that this moon is about abundance, growth, and connection—perfect themes for an evening on the water. Event Details • Strawberry Moon Paddle / Pedal • Sunday, June 28, 2026 • 7:30–9:30 pm $60 per person includes: Hobie pedal kayak, experienced guide, PFD, all gear, and summer moonlight on the river. title: Petaluma Art & Garden Festival
location: Historic Downtown Petaluma,20 4th St, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Petaluma Art & Garden Festival

The Art & Garden festival is one of Petaluma's most loved events! Join us Sunday, July 12, 2026 from 11 am to 5 pm for a fun filled day for all the family. Local crafters, artisans, gardeners, live music on two stages, and an array of local wineries, breweries, restaurants, and fine food purveyors will be participating.

The Art & Garden Festival will take place on Kentucky Street, Fourth Street, B Street, and A Street parking lot. Event Headquarters are at 20 4th Street, Petaluma.

This event is free to attend with Tasting Packages available to those who wish to partake in all the great wine, craft beer, cider, cocktails, and more.

Not the typical street fair, vendors are handpicked and will be showcasing quality, creative home and garden décor, jewelry, arts, and more. With over 100 booths of unusual, unique, handmade items, this event has something for everyone’s taste and budget.

Experts will be on hand to answer gardening questions. Figure out how to grow vegetables in tricky Petaluma adobe soil and what makes a garden organic.

While parents are eating and dancing, kids can enjoy the children’s corner, with jumpy, face painting, FREE hands-on arts and crafts, and more!

Visit http://PetalumaDowntown.com for more information!

title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!

title: SANDCASTLE DRAMA CAMP - Puss In Boots Theme
location: Polly Klaas Community Theater, 417 Western Avenue, Petaluma, CA, 94952, United States
description:
What: Kids explore the theater-making process through games and activities that build creativity, collaboration, and confidence. Each Sandcastle Drama Camp session explores a different story theme, the campers re-write the script as an ensemble to incorporate all their *original creative ideas for story, character, and design* resulting in a completely unique final play for performance each week.

Discounts & Flexible Pricing (sliding scale) available to all. Please complete a form and we will confirm your discount code via email https://forms.gle/QixDYDky7VUUhy6b9

Who: Kids ages 6-12

Program led by Sandcastle Theater Company's professional teaching artists
Approx. 16 students per weekly session (1:8 student/staff ratio)

Where: Polly Klaas Community Theater, 417 Western Ave. Petaluma, CA
When: Monday – Friday, 9am – 3pm

June 8 – 12 — make-your-own-play! Theme: The Princess & the Pea
July 6 – 10 — make-your-own-play! Theme: Alice in Wonderland
July 27 – 31 — make-your-own-play! Puss in Boots

Final Performances: Families and invited guests join us for a staged-reading/performance at 2:30pm on last day of the session.
Daily Schedule:

9am check-in/drop-off
9:30am warm-up games
10am session activities
10:30am snack
10:45am session activities
12pm lunch
12:30pm session activities
1:30pm recess
1:45pm session activities
3pm check-out/pick-up

Notes:

Kids bring their own lunch, water bottle, snacks

title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!
